The target interfaces and fail-closed audits described here are **not yet the

## Product promise

An automatic diagram is useful for Agent-authored circuits only when it does
more than look plausible. A successful `CircuitDiagramResult` must certify
that the visible electrical and semantic projection can be reconstructed and
matched exactly to the `CircuitPlan` snapshot from which it was made.

The promise has three deliberately separate parts:

| Audit | Question | Product responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| A. Electrical fidelity | Do the emitted symbols, pins, wires, ground returns, Ports, and coupled branches reconstruct the exact Plan connectivity? | Mandatory independent renderer audit. |
| B. Semantic fidelity | Do the visible Subsystems, parallel relations, single- or multi-terminal interfaces, and mutual couplings reconstruct the intended presentation IR? | Mandatory independent renderer audit and complete visual alphabet. |
| C. Design intent | Is this exact Plan the circuit the Human intended the Agent to build? | Human review of the certified diagram and review table. |

Passing A and B means that the diagram does not lie about the Plan. It does not
mean that the Plan itself satisfies a Design Target. SCNSim must not describe C
as an automated validation result.

## Authority and snapshot identity

`CircuitPlan` remains the only physical-authoring authority. Layout objects,
diagram geometry, labels, SVG metadata, and audit tables cannot declare a
component, split a net, add a pin, or change canonical ground.

`render_schematic()` captures the same canonical Plan document and SHA-256
encoding used when a later `CircuitRun` seals the Plan. Capturing that immutable
snapshot does not seal or mutate a Plan that is still being authored. If the
Plan changes afterward, the old diagram continues to identify the old
snapshot; a new render receives a new Plan SHA. A diagram and an analysis
result refer to the same physical Plan only when their complete
`plan_sha256` values agree.

The existing Plan SHA binds the physical baseline declaration, including
component hierarchy, topology, the canonical union of grounded endpoints,
canonical SI parameter values, Ports, and couplings. It continues to use the
existing canonical SI encoder unchanged. Source-unit spelling and separate
`ground()` call grouping are provenance facts only; representation, Theme,
layout, and diagram geometry are presentation facts only. None enters Plan
identity. Every grounded endpoint still reconstructs to the one canonical
Plan ground.

## One certification shell, two projection pipelines

Authoring and compiled diagrams share the same fail-closed certification
architecture, not one lowering or one semantic IR:

```text
canonical Plan snapshot
├─> expected authoring manifests
│   authoring semantic lowering -> placement -> routing -> emitted authoring scene
│                                                         ├─> authoring A witness
│                                                         └─> authoring B witness
└─> compiler-expanded graph -> expected compiled manifests
    compiled lowering -> placement -> routing -> emitted compiled scene
                                             ├─> compiled A witness
                                             └─> compiled B witness
                                                                  |
                                                         Theme / SVG serialization
```

The expected authoring manifests are derived directly from the canonical Plan
snapshot. Expected compiled manifests are derived from its exact expanded
graph. The observed manifests are reconstructed from a neutral emitted scene,
after placement and routing, rather than from answer tables retained by the
lowering. The reconstruction code may read only:

- native-symbol types and their transformed electrical anchors;
- CPW/MTL boundary anchors and conductor rows;
- conductive segment endpoints;
- Port boundary, circuit, and load anchors;
- ground-glyph attachment buses;
- T-junction and wire-jump geometry;
- visible relation buses/brackets, stitch marks, coupling marks, and their
  emitted terminals;
- emitted SubsystemRegion boundaries, headers, identity anchors, and
  multi-terminal bracket marks; and
- visible IDs, parameter labels, and coupling marks.

It must not reuse placement, membership, ownership, interface, or attachment
answer tables. One lowered table cannot be both the drawing instruction and
its own witness. Hidden SVG metadata may carry provenance, but it cannot repair
an incomplete visible projection or satisfy either audit.

## Semantic layout IR

The private IR separates electrical identity from drawing geometry.

### ElementBlock

Every authoring physical R, L, C, Josephson junction, and independent junction
capacitance is an orientation-aware native `ElementBlock`. Composite
occurrences recursively expose these native leaves in the authoring
projection. Conductance `G` exists only in the compiled RLGC/pi-ladder
projection and is not an authoring-catalog primitive. A block owns:

- the full component path and primitive kind;
- ordered physical pins and electrical anchors;
- the native Schemdraw symbol bounds;
- separately measured name and baseline-value label rows; and
- one occupied bounding box that includes the required clearances.

Native labels are attached to their oriented symbols. They are not placed as
free-floating text after layout, and label width never stretches the
electrical symbol. Horizontal elements use top or bottom label regions;
vertical elements use the measured outside left or right region appropriate to
their direction. Name and value are measured as separate rows with at least
`1/8 U` between their occupied bounds.

### SubsystemBlock

A `SubsystemBlock` preserves component hierarchy, attachment ownership, and
relative packing. The Subsystem tree contains exactly:

1. the root `CircuitPlan`;
2. every built-in or user-authored Composite occurrence; and
3. every CPW/MTL transmission-line occurrence.

The parent of a non-root Subsystem is the nearest strict Composite ancestor in
its canonical component path, or the Plan root when no such ancestor exists.
Every native leaf is owned by its nearest enclosing Subsystem. Local public
pins carry an explicit boundary-to-parent pin or net mapping at every
Composite boundary; ownership is never flattened through that mapping. A
CPW/MTL block is a terminal boxed electrical Subsystem and owns its ordered
conductor anchors rather than an authoring expansion. All other built-in and
user-authored Composites expand recursively to native R/L/C/JJ/Cj symbols. A
CPW/MTL transmission line is therefore the only boxed electrical symbol. A
Plan-level primitive remains owned by the root while the parent-scope
classification below assigns it exactly one internal or interface
presentation role. A same-scope parent-owned shunt remains outside every child
region. No leaf, relation, or line occurrence may appear in two Subsystems.

A Subsystem is an authored assembly boundary, not an inferred physical mode,
research intent, or topology cluster. Every Composite Subsystem emits a
visible non-conductive `SubsystemRegion` with a measured occupied extent,
boundary, reserved header, and identity anchor; it is never an opaque
electrical box. The root instead emits the unique outermost non-conductive
scene envelope and a reserved root-region kind. Its Plan-identity header is
the optional provenance band controlled by `show_provenance`, not a duplicate
always-visible root header. Composite regions follow component-path nesting;
sibling regions are disjoint. Their colors use deterministic paired pastel
categorical values from a 20-color family in canonical sibling order, but
header and boundary—not color—establish identity and containment. Each
Composite ID is visible exactly once in its header, and a CPW/MTL
electrical-box title supplies its Subsystem ID. When root provenance is
hidden, the scene envelope remains but no Plan-ID header is emitted. Native
leaves use the shortest name unique inside their owning region plus a separate
value row. Full canonical paths remain in the audit table and `run.explain()`.

Hidden child handles remain unavailable to authoring code even though the
sealed physical branches are visible. Visible identity, boundary, and
containment provide the semantic-ownership witness; neither fill color nor a
private placement record is sufficient.

### RelationBlock

Within one owning Subsystem, parallel leaves with the same canonical unordered
endpoint pair form one `RelationBlock`. Examples include C parallel with L and
a Josephson junction parallel with its Cj. A RelationBlock owns its two
terminal buses, native leaves, labels, and any local ground glyph. Relation
formation precedes interface classification, so a parent-owned RelationBlock
may subsequently be one interface member without duplicating its leaves. A
remaining nonparallel primitive is classified once by the same parent-scope
rules. This prevents parallel branches from being placed as a false series
chain.

### InterfaceBundle and attachments

An `InterfaceBundle` is a parent-scope, Plan-derived hyperedge; it is not a
second topology declaration. At each parent scope the renderer applies this
ordered partition:

1. Form every owner-local `RelationBlock`. Before connector traversal, separate
   parent-owned grounded shunts and grounded peripheral relations from the
   member graph. For example, in `A-R1-x-R2-B` with `C(x, ground)`, the two
   resistors may participate in the A-to-B connector while the capacitor
   remains a parent-internal peripheral relation; ground never becomes a peer.
2. Mark boundary nets at immediate-child public-pin sites, CPW/MTL head/tail
   conductor sites, exposed parent-scope pins, and Port-only boundary sites.
   Traversal stops at those nets, at canonical ground, and at every child
   interior.
3. From the remaining parent-owned primitives and RelationBlocks, form each
   initial member component as a **maximal** connected component through
   parent-owned nets that are neither boundary nets nor ground. Preserve every
   exact boundary-site incidence on that component.
4. Classify a component with zero or one distinct peer, or only return sites on
   the same peer, as parent-internal or peripheral. A component incident to two
   or more distinct peers is an interface candidate.
5. For candidates with exactly the same two-peer signature, repeatedly merge
   every pair that shares at least one boundary net until the mandatory maximal
   transitive closure is reached. The closure never traverses a peer interior,
   never crosses a nonshared boundary net, and never merges different peer
   signatures.
6. A component incident to three or more distinct peers remains one
   irreducible multi-party `InterfaceBundle`. Its physical branches are not
   duplicated into fictitious pairwise interfaces.
7. At every boundary net, a direct co-location of two or more boundary sites
   with zero intervening member becomes a separate memberless
   stitch-incidence record. It remains present even when a parent-owned
   capacitor, RelationBlock, or other member-bearing connector also touches
   that same net; member-bearing connectivity cannot absorb the zero-member
   site-to-site incidence.

The result is a neighbor-aware partition rather than one page-wide
topology-connected star. A feedline-to-readout connector and a
readout-to-floating connector remain separate. Two readout capacitors attached
to the floating plus/minus sites form one multi-terminal neighbor bundle when
the required two-peer closure above coalesces them. Disconnected
channels with the same peers but no shared boundary net remain separate. A
parent-owned shunt or same-peer return remains internal to the parent scope and
outside child ownership.

A peer key is one of: an immediate child Subsystem occurrence; an exposed
parent-boundary site keyed by its parent scope and public pin, even when its
internal node is anonymous; or a Port-only boundary keyed by Port identity.
The peer signature is the canonically ordered set of distinct incident peer
keys. An ordinary named Public node at the Plan root does not by itself create
a peer. The signature describes incidence only, not current direction or
inferred function.

Ports co-located with a Subsystem boundary decorate that endpoint. Their full
electrical load, role, and orientation remain visible evidence, but they do not
create another peer. A root endpoint containing only a Port remains
representable through its Port peer key. Panel grouping respects authored
composition and declared non-conductive mutual coupling without ever merging
conductive nets.

Every parent-owned physical leaf first belongs to exactly one primitive or
`RelationBlock`, then is classified exactly once as parent-internal/peripheral
or as a member of exactly one `InterfaceBundle`. The final classifier is the
peer-incidence partition above, not a vague test that a branch merely crosses a
boundary site. Nodes may be referenced by several relation or stitch records
without splitting the node or duplicating a leaf. An attachment-site identity
is not electrical-net equivalence: several sites may share one net, and one
aggregate may expose several sites. A public `CoordinateRef` is
analysis-coordinate evidence, not an electrical boundary site. No interface
rule may invent a node, pin, member, peer, or attachment.

The canonical bundle identity includes its parent scope, peer signature,
canonically sorted endpoint-site identities, members, and canonical node
identities. The visible compact ID is derived from the endpoint Subsystem,
Port, or exposed parent-boundary public-pin IDs. If several bundles have the
same visible participants, a deterministic ordinal sorted by canonical member,
node, and site key disambiguates them. The complete identity remains in the
audit table.

Attachment geometry is decided per derived bundle endpoint site, not from the
total number of neighbors of a whole Subsystem. Multi-terminal status counts
the declared terminal-site identities; every identity remains distinct even
when several sites share one canonical net. Sites on that same canonical net
may share a short conductive bus. Sites on distinct nets remain electrically
separate and are grouped only by a visible non-conductive bracket and
`InterfaceBundle` ID. For a multi-party bundle, each participant's sites face
the common connector region rather than a nonexistent single peer. Three or
more co-net attachments use a short ordered bus, never a forced center star;
distinct-net attachments never do. Route constraints may choose an eligible
side or order but cannot redefine this partition.

The renderer certifies only single-terminal versus multi-terminal structure.
It never infers a differential pair from IDs, geometry, electrical symmetry,
or a later `transform_pair()` request. Differential meaning remains a Human
Design Target interpretation until a separate authoring-semantic scope defines
explicit physical metadata.

### NetBus and NetTap

One `ElectricNode` may need several geometric contacts. The layout may
therefore create one private `NetBus` with several private `NetTap` anchors.
All taps reconstruct to the same electrical node. A labeled Public node has
one identity anchor and one filled dot; ordinary taps and T-junctions are
unfilled. A Port-promoted node is identified by its open Port circle rather
than a second node dot.

## Complete visual alphabet

### Native branches and ground

Authoring R, L, C, Josephson junctions, and Cj are drawn with native electrical
symbols. Compiled RLGC leaves additionally use native G symbols. IDC is shown
as its terminal-to-terminal capacitance plus both
terminal-to-reference shunts. Grounded and floating resonators expose their
actual parallel branches. A SQUID exposes both junctions, each Cj, and finite
loop inductance.

Within one owning Subsystem, parallel grounded branches attached to the same
signal node share a short local bottom bus and one ground glyph. Shunts in
different Subsystems or on different signal nodes receive separate ground
glyphs even though every glyph maps to the one canonical Plan ground.
`ground()` call grouping is shown only as source provenance in the audit table;
it cannot merge or split visual buses. Canonical ground is never a page-wide
layout vertex or rail.

### CPW and MTL

One-conductor transmission line is an inline CPW box with continuous outline,
input/output anchors, ID, and length. Multi-conductor line is one MTL box with
ordered conductor rows and one head/tail anchor per row. The reference
conductor is explicit legend metadata and never creates an inferred ground
wire.

The compiled projection expands every line into its complete pi ladder. For
N>1 it preserves matrix order and complete C/G and L/R evidence rather than
inventing scalar equivalents.

### Logical Ports

A logical Port is one rotatable presentation block containing:

- an open boundary circle;
- an interior circuit anchor;
- an unfilled interior T-junction;
- the declared reference-impedance branch and local ground; and
- a visible Port ID, role, and baseline Z0.

`terminated` and `nonloading_probe` are visibly distinct; the latter is marked
PTC-removable. The load branch is the existing raw-network Port load, not an
authored Library resistor. On an interior horizontal bus the Port block faces
top or bottom; on an interior vertical bus it faces left or right. Endpoint
Ports may remain tangent to the bus.

### Junctions and crossings

- A filled dot denotes one labeled Public-node identity.
- An ordinary same-net T-junction is unfilled.
- A same-net four-way meeting becomes two staggered T-junctions.
- Different nets never use an ordinary cross; an unavoidable crossing uses a
  wire jump.
- Wires may enter or leave blocks only through registered anchors and may not
  cross a symbol, label, or Port block. A wire may occupy its owning Subsystem
  region and cross an intended Subsystem boundary only through a registered
  attachment anchor; an unrelated wire may not traverse that region.

### CouplingRelation and mutual inductance

Every declared mutual inductance becomes one non-conductive
`CouplingRelation`, separate from conductive InterfaceBundles. Its two oriented
inductive branches retain their nearest Subsystem owners. The relation itself
is owned by the lowest common ancestor of those owners; it is internal when
both owners match and cross-Subsystem otherwise. Its canonical identity binds
that owner, both oriented branch identities, and signed `k`. Neither case
changes electrical nets.

When both inductors participate only in one coupling and can remain adjacent
without changing public-terminal order or violating occupied boxes, they are
drawn as adjacent parallel inductors with signed `k` between them and derived
`M` when values are visible.

Otherwise the diagram contains a non-optional coupling legend that identifies
both oriented branch paths, signed `k`, and optional derived `M`. A mutual
coupling with neither an adjacent mark nor a complete visible legend fails the
semantic audit. This same rule applies to every declared SQUID-arm or loop
coupling; proximity never implies an undeclared `k`, and no declared `k` may be
left implicit. Drawing placement never determines the physical sign.

## Automatic placement and routing

All geometry derives from one private diagram metric system with
`unit_length = 2.2` Schemdraw coordinates:

| Quantity | Minimum |
|---|---|
| Native element span | `1 U` |
| Label clearance | `1/8 U` |
| Terminal stub and wire obstacle clearance | `1/4 U` |
| Routing-lane pitch | `1/2 U` |
| Port lead | `5/8 U` |
| Port load span | `1 U` |
| Grounded-branch depth | `2 U` |
| Disconnected-panel gap | `3 U` |

Measured symbol, label, legend, and provenance bounds may only increase these
spacings. No fixture ID, Tutorial name, component ID, hand-authored coordinate,
or public scale knob may bypass the metric system.

Each connected panel is decomposed into articulation and biconnected blocks
after constructing its Subsystem/Relation/Interface quotient graph. The
weighted diameter of the resulting block-cut tree supplies a deterministic
reading spine; it maximizes covered Subsystem and Interface blocks, then uses
canonical component paths and exact IDs as tie breakers, never component
declaration order. A biconnected cycle stays one semantic block and chooses its
internal orientation by the same canonical ordering rather than being broken
into a false tree.

Ports are boundary sites attached after that semantic spine exists. A
`terminated` role may prefer an exterior inline side and a
`nonloading_probe` role prefers a peripheral side, but neither role, Port
count, nor first declaration may define topology or select the root. A panel
with no InterfaceBundle lays out its root-owned relations by the same
block-cut rule. Disconnected circuits are packed as separate panels. Panel
grouping preserves authored composition and declared mutual-coupling evidence;
it never merges electrically distinct nets.

Placement reserves complete ElementBlock, RelationBlock, InterfaceBundle,
Port, label, and legend bounds. Rows, columns, boundary buses, and routing lanes
are selected from a finite, deterministically ordered candidate set derived
from graph size, measured occupied bounds, canonical paths, and exact IDs. An
explicit side/order conflict or exhaustion of that finite set fails
`schematic_layout`; there is no unbounded grow-and-retry success claim. The
heuristic does not claim a global optimum, and V1 exposes no drawing-size,
threshold, or layout-scale knob.

## Pre-render catalog and Root-only manual hints

Manual V1 is a constrained reading-order input to the same automatic engine.
It is Root-only and is not a coordinate escape hatch. Nested Subsystems always
lay out automatically and remain fully audited.

`plan.schematic_catalog()` derives one immutable, non-mutating
`SchematicCatalog` snapshot before rendering. It neither seals nor edits the
Plan. `catalog.show()` is an explicitly **Plan-derived / UNCERTIFIED** lookup
surface for participants, interfaces, sites, and incidence; it is not a
diagram audit and contains no observations from emitted geometry.
The catalog and every ref bind the captured `plan_sha256` plus the catalog
schema identity.

The catalog exposes only typed opaque handles:

- `catalog.participant(public_handle)` returns a
  `SchematicParticipantRef` only for an immediate Subsystem occurrence under
  the Plan root or for a root boundary/Port participant that actually exists
  in the derived graph. A primitive coupler is member evidence for
  `find_interface`, not a participant; an ordinary root Public node, a hidden
  child, or a nested Subsystem is not made eligible merely because it has a
  public-looking handle;
- `catalog.find_interface(members=(), nodes=())` intersects the supplied
  public evidence and must match exactly one already-derived relation. A
  member-bearing lookup requires nonempty `members`; optional `nodes` further
  intersects that lookup. With empty `members`, nonempty `nodes` selects only a
  complete memberless stitch and can never select a co-located member-bearing
  bundle. It returns a `SchematicInterfaceRef` and never declares a new
  interface; and
- `catalog.attachment(interface, participant=..., pin=None)` returns a
  `SchematicAttachmentRef` for one existing aggregate site. The public pin
  selector is optional and only disambiguates an existing aggregate, including
  an MTL head/tail conductor aggregate. It cannot split conductors or
  terminals.

Both collections empty, duplicate evidence, hidden or ineligible handles, and
zero, several, or conflicting matches fail closed. An anonymous stitch without
complete public node evidence remains automatic-only. Refs from repeated
catalogs are mutually usable only when both the unchanged Plan snapshot and
catalog schema identities agree. A changed Plan makes earlier refs stale; a
different schema, foreign catalog, or ref outside the root-visible eligibility
boundary is rejected rather than reinterpreted.

`SchematicRoute(through=(...), via=(...))` contains at least two ordered
`SchematicParticipantRef`s and exactly one intervening
`SchematicInterfaceRef` per adjacent participant pair. Every `via` must
already be incident to both neighbors. The route states left-to-right reading
order only: it does not claim a unique conductive path or current direction,
and it cannot discard an internal cycle. The authoring graph is undirected;
IDs, names, component roles, and Port roles never imply flow.

`catalog.layout(primary_routes=..., attachment_sides=...,
attachment_order=..., port_sides=...)` is the only layout factory.
`primary_routes` contains
`SchematicRoute`s. `attachment_sides` maps `SchematicAttachmentRef` keys to
`DiagramSide`; `attachment_order` maps a `SchematicParticipantRef` to an
ordered tuple of its incident `SchematicAttachmentRef`s; and `port_sides` maps
Port-backed `SchematicParticipantRef` keys to `DiagramSide`. The factory
copies every input mapping, validates root-scope eligibility and all conflicts,
and returns a frozen `SchematicLayout`. Manual V1 rejects nested participants
or attachments because nested Subsystems remain fully automatic. Raw strings,
foreign or stale refs, nonincident attachments, impossible sides,
contradictory routes, incomplete route incidence, and conflicting orders fail
before placement. Route or side constraints may arrange only existing
participants, interfaces, and attachments; they cannot change ownership,
partitioning, incidence, or electrical topology.

The following **TARGET scaffold is intentionally not executable in the current
runtime**. It assumes `left_lc` and `right_lc` are two public Composite handles,
`coupling_capacitor` is their parent-owned coupler, `port_in` and `port_out` are
terminated Ports decorating the two LC endpoint nodes. Those Ports do not
fabricate separate `InterfaceBundle`s. The scaffold demonstrates every manual
layout input without making a runtime availability claim:

```python
# TARGET API — two authored LC Composites, one coupler, and terminated Ports.
from scnsim import CircuitDiagramSpec, DiagramSide, SchematicRoute

catalog = plan.schematic_catalog()
catalog.show()

port_in_ref = catalog.participant(public_handle=port_in)
left_lc_ref = catalog.participant(public_handle=left_lc)
right_lc_ref = catalog.participant(public_handle=right_lc)
port_out_ref = catalog.participant(public_handle=port_out)

coupler_if = catalog.find_interface(
    members=(coupling_capacitor,),
    nodes=(),
)
left_coupler_attachment = catalog.attachment(
    interface=coupler_if,
    participant=left_lc_ref,
    pin=None,
)
right_coupler_attachment = catalog.attachment(
    interface=coupler_if,
    participant=right_lc_ref,
    pin=None,
)

layout = catalog.layout(
    primary_routes=(
        SchematicRoute(
            through=(left_lc_ref, right_lc_ref),
            via=(coupler_if,),
        ),
    ),
    attachment_sides={
        left_coupler_attachment: DiagramSide.RIGHT,
        right_coupler_attachment: DiagramSide.LEFT,
    },
    attachment_order={
        left_lc_ref: (left_coupler_attachment,),
        right_lc_ref: (right_coupler_attachment,),
    },
    port_sides={
        port_in_ref: DiagramSide.LEFT,
        port_out_ref: DiagramSide.RIGHT,
    },
)

diagram = plan.render_schematic(CircuitDiagramSpec(layout=layout))
```

`plan.render_schematic()` remains the zero-hint convenience and invokes the
same catalog builder. Hinted and zero-hint renders traverse the same placement,
routing, neutral-scene emission, and independent audits. For one Plan snapshot
and representation their connectivity, semantic, and expanded-graph digests
are identical; presentation layout may differ. `diagram.audit` remains
reserved for the certificate and observed reconstruction table—there is no
duplicate catalog API on the audit.

These target surfaces replace user-constructed Interface/Attachment objects,
`SchematicPath`, `SchematicGroup`, and `branch_order` completely. There is no
alias, compatibility encoder, or migration path. Compiled diagrams reject
authoring layout hints.

## Independent audits and digests

### Electrical reconstruction (A)

The observed electrical manifest normalizes:

- every native branch kind, component path plus branch role, terminal evidence,
  and reconstructed net;
- every ground return to canonical Plan ground;
- every Port attachment, role, Z0, and node-to-reference orientation;
- every CPW/MTL conductor, reference, head/tail attachment, and row order;
- every CouplingRelation's mutually coupled oriented branch pair; and
- every visible exact-zero omission record, including the omitted branch role
  or compiled term, its endpoints, checked absence, and surviving-path
  continuity evidence.

Its canonical digest is `connectivity_sha256`. The observed manifest must
equal the independently generated expected manifest exactly; set equality
without complete terminal and orientation evidence is insufficient. The
declared physical pin order remains unchanged. Comparison may normalize the
terminal swap of a reciprocal R or C, or another symmetry explicitly proven by
its component model; symmetry is closed by default and is never inferred from
symbol shape. Reversal is tested only after that permitted normalization.
Orientation-sensitive branches, mutual-coupling branch order, JJ orientation,
and CPW/MTL head/tail still fail on reversal and retain visible direction
evidence. A JJ and its parallel Cj are separate physical leaves because their
branch roles differ even when their endpoints agree. There is no universal
semantic meaning assigned to labels such as `terminal_1` and `terminal_2`.

Anonymous-net equivalence is reconstructed from complete endpoint sets, never
from a hidden ID or a layout-generated name. A missing visible term cannot be
interpreted as numerical zero. Expected authoring omissions come from the
canonical Plan snapshot plus existing exact-zero component rules, such as an
explicitly omitted zero Cj. Expected compiled omissions come from the expanded
graph evidence. A visible omission record must identify the branch role or
compiled term and endpoints, then prove its absence and the required surviving
continuity; the drawing never infers an omission from missing ink and adds no
near-zero threshold.

### Semantic reconstruction (B)

The authoring observed semantic manifest reconstructs:

- the unique root role and nested SubsystemRegions, their visible non-root
  identities, and their parent/child containment;
- every leaf owner by requiring its whole occupied symbol-and-label box to lie
  inside its reconstructed owning region and outside every child region, then
  combining that region path with its unique local name;
- RelationBlock endpoints and native members;
- InterfaceBundle parent scope, endpoint sites, member branches, Public nodes,
  peer signature, single- versus multi-terminal classification, and visible
  bracket/bus identity;
- separate memberless stitch incidences;
- Port-boundary ownership; and
- CouplingRelation branch ownership, presentation mode, and visible identity.

Its canonical digest is `semantic_sha256`. A parallel relation drawn as series,
a multi-terminal interface drawn as unrelated single-terminal branches, an
omitted coupling mark, a leaf box crossing into a child region, or an ambiguous
ownership region or label fails this audit even when electrical connectivity
happens to be correct. The witness reads emitted SubsystemRegions, complete
occupied boxes, and identity anchors; it cannot read the placement ownership
table. Only registered electrical attachment crossings may cross a region
boundary. Adjacent-inductor and visible-legend coupling presentations normalize
to the same coupling identity; their geometric presentation mode is audit
evidence but is not part of the semantic digest. All observed relations come
from emitted endpoints, anchors, region boundaries, and visible marks—not from
the expected partition.

### Geometry and label validity

Before semantic serialization, layout validation proves that occupied blocks
and labels do not overlap, wires contact only registered anchors, conductive
paths are continuous, and junction/jump grammar is unambiguous. When baseline
values are visible, each uses a deterministic engineering SI prefix derived
from the canonical value. Source-unit spelling is not reconstructed from the
displayed value; when retained, it appears separately only as verified snapshot
provenance and is never substituted for the canonical value.

Theme, hint choice, provenance visibility, padding, and equivalent geometric
routing are excluded from the Plan, connectivity, and semantic digest
preimages. The `connectivity_sha256` and `semantic_sha256` preimages each
include their `authoring` or `compiled` representation tag and a schema-tagged
canonical encoding. Invariance is required across Theme and hints within one
representation; authoring and compiled connectivity or semantic digests are
not required to match one another. Plan identity, compiled lineage,
expanded-graph identity, and optional presentation identity retain their own
encoders described on this page; no universal representation-tag rule is
asserted for every digest. Diagram digests never redefine existing Plan or
request encoders.

## Target Result and presentation surface

The target defaults make an ordinary authoring diagram review-ready. This is a
syntactically valid target usage example, not a claim that the target API is
already implemented:

```python
from scnsim import CircuitDiagramSpec, Theme

diagram_spec = CircuitDiagramSpec(
    representation="authoring",
    theme=Theme.AUTO,
    show_parameter_values=True,
    show_provenance=True,
    layout=None,  # SchematicLayout | None
)
diagram = plan.render_schematic(diagram_spec)
```

Successful construction attaches an immutable audit with no public
constructor. The following is its read-only protocol, not a user-constructible
dataclass:

```python
class CircuitDiagramAudit:
    @property
    def representation(self) -> Literal["authoring", "compiled"]: ...

    @property
    def plan_id(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def plan_sha256(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def connectivity_sha256(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def semantic_sha256(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def compiled_graph_sha256(self) -> str | None: ...

    @property
    def expanded_graph_sha256(self) -> str | None: ...

    @property
    def presentation_sha256(self) -> str | None: ...

    def show(self) -> HtmlPresentation: ...

diagram.audit.plan_sha256
diagram.audit.connectivity_sha256
diagram.audit.semantic_sha256
diagram.audit.compiled_graph_sha256
diagram.audit.expanded_graph_sha256
diagram.audit.presentation_sha256
diagram.audit.show()
```

There is no `passed` boolean: failure returns no diagram or audit object.
Successful certification freezes one checked scene.
`CircuitDiagramResult.show()` still returns a real Schemdraw `Drawing` through
a supported read-only subclass/facade; callers cannot mutate the scene behind
its certificate. Existing `Drawing.save()` remains the static API; this scope
adds no save or export API. `show()`, rich display, and `Drawing.save()` all
serialize that same frozen scene, so no later mutation can leave a stale
certificate. Notebook rich display retains its self-contained
copy, zoom, reset, drag-pan, and Open SVG surface, with a readable static SVG
fallback.

`presentation_sha256` is optional. When present, it identifies the canonical
frozen scene while excluding its self-referential certificate annotation. It
is a presentation identity, not an authenticity or security signature, and it
does not enter Plan, request, connectivity, semantic, or expanded-graph
identity.

### Provenance region

A measured bottom provenance band and outer padding keep all symbols and labels
away from the image boundary. By default the band displays:

```text
AUTHORING · CircuitPlan <id> · plan <12> · conn <12> · semantic <12> · values: baseline
```

A compiled diagram additionally displays `compiler <12> · expanded <12>`.
The provenance band uses the same Theme palette as the drawing. Complete
digests remain in `CircuitDiagramAudit` and SVG metadata; neither independent
audit relies on that metadata.

`show_provenance=False` removes the visible provenance band, not the root scene
envelope, and never disables the audits or typed certificate. A copied raster
without the band consequently has no standalone visible provenance; this is
an explicit presentation choice. The hidden-band form cannot be the sole
code-free Human acceptance packet.

### Audit review table

`diagram.audit.show()` displays the audited observed reconstruction rather than
printing the Plan's expected manifest a second time. It separates **observed
scene facts** from **verified snapshot/provenance facts**. Observed rows contain:

- Public nodes, exact endpoints, and canonical-ground returns;
- Ports, roles, Z0, and orientation;
- InterfaceBundle peers, sites, members, and multi-terminal marks;
- memberless stitch incidences;
- RelationBlock endpoints and native leaves;
- mutual-coupling branch identities and signed `k`, plus derived `M` only when
  it was emitted and independently checked against the bound values;
- CPW/MTL conductor order, reference, and head/tail attachments;
- visible exact-zero omissions and continuity evidence; and
- displayed baseline values.

Verified rows contain Plan/schema and complete digest identities, canonical SI
values (including hidden baseline values), source-unit spelling, source
`ground()` call groups, and other hidden snapshot provenance. Ground-call
groups are explicitly excluded from geometry and every diagram digest input;
source-unit spelling is excluded from Plan and diagram semantic identity. When
derived `M` is not emitted, any snapshot-derived value belongs only in these
verified rows and is not reported as an observed scene fact.

For a compiled projection it also includes the expanded graph identity, line
sections, conductor/station identities, complete matrix evidence, and omitted
compiled zero terms.

## Compiled projection

Compiled diagrams use the same expected-versus-observed witness architecture
but never reuse authoring Subsystem, InterfaceBundle, attachment, or placement
rules. They perform two representation-specific certified comparisons:

```text
Plan snapshot -> compiler expanded graph -> expected compiled manifest
                                  actual compiled drawing
                                           -> observed compiled manifest
```

The Plan SHA proves the physical source. Existing runtime
`compiled_graph_sha256` identifies Plan-plus-Julia-source lineage; it is not a
content digest of the expansion. The distinct `expanded_graph_sha256` binds
`plan_sha256` together with the disclosed structural content: `node_order`,
`resolved_bindings`, and `expanded_branch_rows`, using the existing runtime
encoder unchanged. It does not claim to cover every derived stamp matrix.
The compiled electrical witness reconstructs emitted primitive
pins, nets, line stations, sections, and ordered conductor rows. Its semantic
witness reconstructs compiler hierarchy, pi-section membership, matrix-entry
provenance, and omitted-zero records. The representation-tagged connectivity
and semantic digests prove the visible compiled drawing; they are not aliases
for the authoring digests. A large ladder may use deterministic pages or
panels, but it cannot truncate sections, conductor rows, matrix entries,
attachments, or omitted-zero evidence.

Compiled projection remains structural baseline evidence. It contains no PTC,
retain, transform, Schur reduction, Direct/HB response, or ParameterSet
override. Those request-specific facts belong to `run.explain()` and verified
analysis Results.

The A/B comparisons establish structural correspondence between the expected
snapshot or expansion and the observed scene. They do not prove that the
trusted baseline compiler or solver is scientifically correct, and they do not
cover ParameterSet overrides, selected Views, PTC, or numerical results.

## Fail-closed behavior

Layout cannot return a degraded or partial image. These are
`schematic_layout` failures:

- malformed, foreign, ambiguous, or contradictory manual hints;
- an unplaceable required visual mark or provenance region;
- symbol, Port, label, legend, or panel overlap;
- a wire entering a non-anchor obstacle;
- a disconnected required wire segment; or
- an ambiguous ordinary crossing that cannot be represented with the junction
  and jump alphabet.

These are `schematic_audit` failures:

- expected and reconstructed pins, nets, ground, Ports, or line conductors
  differ;
- a branch is missing, duplicated, attached to the wrong net, or remains
  reversed after every explicitly permitted model-symmetry normalization;
- RelationBlock, InterfaceBundle, Subsystem containment, single- versus
  multi-terminal classification, or CouplingRelation ownership differs;
- a complete leaf symbol-and-label occupied box leaves its owning region,
  enters a child region, or crosses a region boundary other than at a
  registered electrical attachment;
- a required coupling or omission record is not visibly and completely
  represented; or
- a visible baseline name/value label disagrees with the captured Plan.

Both classes raise `SCNSimValidationError` with the named `stage`. They occur
before a `CircuitDiagramResult` exists and never allocate a runtime attempt,
receipt, artifact, or workspace entry. No warning-only path, page-wide-rail
fallback, hidden metadata repair, or best-effort success is allowed.

## Human review protocol

An Agent submitting a `CircuitPlan` supplies a code-free review packet:

1. the default authoring diagram with baseline values and provenance visible;
2. the Net/BOM table from `diagram.audit.show()`;
3. a compiled diagram and compiled audit table when CPW/MTL matrix or
   pi-ladder expansion must be reviewed, especially for `N > 1`; and
4. the applicable Design Target against which the Human judges intent.

Machine audit guarantees A and B. The Human uses the certified visual grammar
to decide C: whether the topology, Subsystems, interfaces, Port roles,
couplings, and baseline quantities are the intended circuit.

## Honest limits

- Diagram values are Plan baselines, not values from a particular
  `ParameterSet`, optimizer candidate, or HB case.
- Authoring and compiled diagrams show the physical Plan. They do not show a
  selected View, PTC compensation, retain, transform, Schur elimination, or
  normalization choice.
- A diagram cannot accept an optimization result, scientific Gate, or Design
  Target.
- `run.explain()` remains the authority for request-specific lowering and
  evidence; it cannot substitute for a visible coupling mark or repair a
  failed diagram audit.
- Matrix RLGC requires its complete compiled table/legend to be reviewed; the
  CPW/MTL authoring box alone is intentionally insufficient.
- Router stress graphs are diagnostic inputs, not product circuit fixtures or
  examples of physical intent.

## Supersession and implementation order

This document is the only current target authority for the affected scope.
The existing renderer and old public hint classes remain temporarily reachable
only because this is a documentation-first convergence checkpoint. Delivery
order remains:

1. complete exact-document review of this full target;
2. align real vertical runtime slices, replacing the old hint API without
   aliases or a compatibility encoder and removing superseded rail,
   opaque-Composite, packing-group, and best-effort paths;
3. validate each coherent implementation slice with non-test probes and
   Human-visible diagrams while retaining one integration scope;
4. request Human acceptance of the exact combined implementation candidate;
   and
5. add durable stabilization tests only after that acceptance.

Until that alignment is complete, current rendered diagrams must not be
described as satisfying this target contract.
